narrative: You are being denied a promotion because the model estimates an 81% chance that you will leave your job. This is not a judgment of your ability; it means the organization believes the risk of investing in you now is too high because you may not stay long enough to justify it. The strongest factor in your profile was your overall experience of one to five years, which actually argued against leaving—many employees predicted to stay share that level. However, it was outweighed by two signals that pushed toward leaving. The next strongest was that you have received other job opportunities while in this role; only about a quarter of employees predicted to stay had such offers, so this strongly increased the estimate. Third, your sector, listed as other, also tilted the prediction toward leaving, as it is less common among employees expected to stay than medical or education. Other details—feeling under-rewarded for effort, not receiving the promotion you felt you deserved, and low job stability—add to that concern. Before denying the promotion permanently, the organization should discuss retention, pay, recognition, and career path with you; otherwise, the prediction may become self-fulfilling.
